items.headline: OpenAI sued by eight US states over ChatGPT safety concerns
items.summary: A coalition of eight states filed separate lawsuits accusing OpenAI of endangering children, deceiving parents, and violating consumer-protection laws through ChatGPT. The suits add to mounting legal and regulatory pressure on OpenAI over product safety as ChatGPT's user base keeps growing.

items.headline: OpenAI says it banned ChatGPT accounts tied to Russian and Iranian influence operations
items.summary: OpenAI disclosed it disrupted covert influence campaigns originating in Russia and Iran that used its AI tools, with the Russian-linked activity reportedly targeting Latin America to undermine support for Ukraine. The disclosure highlights the growing use of generative AI in state-linked disinformation efforts.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5, a cheaper small model with adjustable effort levels
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, pitched as its fastest and most cost-efficient model yet, priced roughly 75% below Haiku 4.5 and built to serve as a subagent under larger Opus and Sonnet models. It is the first Haiku model to offer selectable reasoning-effort tiers from Low to Max.

items.headline: Anthropic gives startups a free year of Claude Team and $1,000 in API credits
items.summary: Anthropic expanded its Claude for Startups program, offering eligible early-stage companies a complimentary year of Claude Team seats plus $1,000 in token credits. The move is aimed at deepening developer adoption as competition for enterprise and startup AI workloads intensifies.

items.headline: Meta launches Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, new agentic AI models
items.summary: Meta introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, frontier models built for sustained personal and professional agent work such as reviewing documents, coding, and specialized tasks in finance, law, and health. Meta claims the models compete with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 on internal benchmarks, underscoring its push to catch up in the agentic-AI race.

items.headline: Elon Musk says Tesla Optimus robot hands are 'shockingly difficult' to build
items.summary: Musk acknowledged that engineering dexterous, reliable robot hands remains one of the biggest obstacles to scaling Optimus production, even as Tesla aims for eventual annual output of a million humanoid robots. The comments underscore how actuator and manipulation hardware, not just AI software, remains a key bottleneck for humanoid robotics.

items.headline: Boston Dynamics details redesigned humanoid hand for Atlas
items.summary: Boston Dynamics shared new details on a redesigned four-fingered, directly actuated hand for its Atlas humanoid, which has 13 degrees of freedom after the company dropped the pinky finger and shrank the gripper. The update reflects an industry-wide push to improve robotic manipulation as humanoids move toward real factory deployments.

items.headline: New 'RSI-Anything' framework pushes toward recursive AI self-improvement using world models
items.summary: Researchers published RSI-Anything, a framework pairing a policy with a predictive world model that ranks candidate actions to cut costly external evaluation, then adapts itself when predictions become unreliable. Reported results include code-repair success rising from 26.3% to 31.2% and lab-planning scores more than doubling, offering an early look at scalable self-improving AI systems.
